sources.title: Dali Erhai Lake: What to See and the Best Way to Visit - China Highlights
sources.content:
Erhai Lake: Complete Text Content

Overview
Erhai Lake stands as one of China's most beautiful lakes and represents the second-largest freshwater lake in Yunnan Province. The Dali people regard it as their "mother lake," essential to their way of life. The name Erhai means "Ear Sea," reflecting the lake's distinctive ear-like shape. This plateau lake appears as a deep blue jewel set within green landscapes, creating spectacular scenery when combined with the Cangshan Mountains, whose peaks often mirror in the water alongside the sun and moon.

Key Attractions and Villages

Shuanglang Town occupies the northeast shore, featuring bluestone walls, stone-paved roads, and narrow alleys with a lively atmosphere. Main attractions include Yuji Island and Nanzhao Folk Island, offering excellent sunset viewing opportunities.

Xizhou Town sits on the west shore, approximately 17 kilometers from Dali Old Town by bicycle. This quieter location showcases "traditional Bai houses" and local specialties like Xizhou baba (Dali-style pancakes) plus local souvenirs.

Wase Village is positioned on the east shore as a beautiful small fishing community. It preserves numerous Bai-style ancient gate towers constructed during the late Qing Dynasty (1644-1912) and early Republic of China era (1912-1949). Hotels with lake views make it an ideal quiet retreat.

Small Putuo Island sits by the east shore. Legend describes it as a seal from Guanyin, the Buddhist goddess of mercy, protecting fishermen. The island features Guanyin Pavilion. Winter brings black-headed gulls from Siberia.

Haidong Town represents a small Bai ethnicity settlement focused on fishing. Along its 19-kilometer southeast shoreline are three shallow bays and two islands, including Jinsuo Island (the largest on Erhai Lake) and Luoquan Peninsula, offering excellent views of both the lake and Cangshan Mountains.

Cycling Around Erhai Lake
The lake stretches approximately 41 kilometers long with widths between 3-9 kilometers. A complete bike circuit measures roughly 120 kilometers.

Haixi Route (West Shore): Beginning at Cai Village near Dali Old Town and extending to Little Forest in Xiaguan District covers about 13 kilometers one-way. Motor vehicles are prohibited on this path, making it suitable for younger or less experienced cyclists.

Haidong Route (East Shore): The optimal section runs from Wase village to Wenbi village, also approximately 13 kilometers one-way. This quieter route provides panoramic mountain and lake views, best experienced in afternoon hours to enjoy the sunset.

Lake Cruises
Cruise routes depart from Xiaguan Pier at Erhai Park, Longkan Pier near Dali Old Town, or Taoyuan Pier. These vessels pass islands like Nanzhao Folk Island and Small Putuo Island, plus Luoquan Peninsula.

Best Visiting Times
Spring and Fall (March-May and September-October) provide ideal conditions with wonderful sunlight and soft breezes. Winter suits seagull watching, with mild daytime temperatures. Summer brings occasional heavy downpours, though rain-free days remain pleasant. Sun protection becomes essential due to strong ultraviolet radiation.

sources.content:
Erhai Lake, Dali, Yunnan

Erhai Lake is one of the most beautiful lakes in China, and it is the second largest freshwater lake in Yunnan Province. The lake covers an area of 250 square kilometers and is located about two kilometers east of Dali. The 136-kilometer ecological cycling route circles much of the lake, making it one of the best cycling destinations in China.

The lake is flanked by Cangshan Mountain to the west, creating stunning scenery. Villages around the lake include Shuanglang, Xizhou, Wase, and Haidong, each offering unique cultural experiences.

Cruises are available from multiple piers. The Dali "Three Tea Ceremony of the Bai Ethnic Group, with Song and Dance Performances" are a special feature of cruise experiences.

Zhoucheng is located on the west side of Erhai Lake and is called the "Land for National Tie-dye" where travelers can learn how to make a tie-dyed cloth.

sources.title: Exploring Erhai Lake in Dali: Must-Do Experiences
sources.content:
Exploring Erhai Lake in Dali: Must-Do Experiences

Erhai Lake is the defining landscape of Dali. A 136-kilometer ecological cycling route circles much of the lake, making it one of the best cycling destinations in China.

Must-do experiences include cycling along the lake shore, taking a lake cruise, visiting lakeside villages like Shuanglang and Xizhou, watching the sunset over the lake, and winter seagull watching.

The west shore (Haixi) offers views of the lake with Cangshan Mountain behind you, while the east shore (Haidong) provides panoramic views of both the lake and the mountain range.

sources.content:
Erhai Lake, Dali: A Serene Escape in Yunnan Province

Erhai Lake is the seventh largest freshwater lake in China and the second largest in Yunnan Province. Located at an elevation of 1,972 meters, the lake is about 42 kilometers long and 3-9 kilometers wide, with a surface area of about 250 square kilometers.

The lake is surrounded by numerous Bai ethnic minority villages, each with its own character and attractions. Popular activities include cycling around the lake, taking boat cruises, visiting fishing villages, and enjoying the natural scenery.

Best times to visit are spring (March-May) for mild weather and autumn (September-October) for clear skies. Winter attracts birdwatchers who come to see migratory Siberian gulls.

sources.title: Strolling Along the Scenic Erhai Lake Park in Dali City, Yunnan - Feastography
sources.content:
Strolling Along the Scenic Erhai Lake Park in Dali City, Yunnan

Erhai Lake Park is located in the southern part of Erhai Lake, near Xiaguan (Dali City). The park provides a peaceful setting for leisurely walks along the lakefront, with views of the water and surrounding mountains.

The park features walking paths, gardens, and viewing platforms. It serves as a starting point for boat cruises on Erhai Lake. The park is free to enter and is popular with both locals and tourists.

The views from the park encompass the expansive lake with Cangshan Mountain visible across the water, creating a classic Dali landscape scene.

sources.title: 洱海 - 百度百科
sources.content:
洱海完整内容

基本信息
洱海位于云南省大理白族自治州大理市境内，是"仅次于滇池的云南第二大湖"。湖水面积约246平方千米，蓄水量约29.5亿立方米，南北长40公里，海拔1972米。

名称演变
古代有"叶榆水"、"叶榆河"、"叶榆泽"、"西洱河"等名称。"洱"字源于其"形若人耳"或"如月抱珥"的形状，"海"的称法源于云南习俗，湖泊多被称作"海"。

地理位置与境域
湖体主要在大理市，北岸连接洱源县东南隅。环湖有双廊、江尾、喜州等镇，泄水口位于西南端下关。

水文特征
湖面年水温1℃-20℃，透明度4米，属中营养型淡水湖，终年不结冰。

三岛
金梭岛：最大岛屿，面积约74万平方米，形似织布梭子
玉几岛：有"苍洱第一村"美誉，保留白族传统民居
赤文岛：半岛形，新旧石器时代遗址，有观音阁、八仙台等景观

沿岸名胜
崇圣寺三塔、蝴蝶泉、南诏德化碑、大理古城等。

气候特征
属中亚热带西南季风气候，年平均气温15.5℃，年降雨量1000-1100毫米，"四季如春"。

生态保护
1981年建立省级自然保护区，1994年晋升国家级。2019年1月起实行全年封湖禁渔。2022年监测到世界极危鸟类青头潜鸭，标志生态恢复。2023年11月入选国家重要湿地名录。

湖区物产
鱼类8科20属33种，土著鱼17种。洱海特有的大理裂腹鱼、洱海鲤为国家二级保护。水生植物26科44属61种。

sources.title: Dali Erhai Lake Travel: Entrance Tickets, Travel Tips, Photos and Maps - Yunnan Exploration
sources.content:
Dali Erhai Lake Travel Guide

Erhai Lake is one of the seven biggest freshwater lakes in China. Located between Dali Old Town and Cangshan Mountain, it is the defining natural feature of the Dali region.

The lake has a surface area of about 250 square kilometers and sits at 1,972 meters elevation. A complete cycling circuit around the lake is approximately 120-136 kilometers.

Popular activities include cycling, boating, visiting lakeside villages, and photography. The lake is free to access, though boat cruises and some island visits require tickets.

Transportation: Multiple options available from Dali Old Town, including bicycle rental, electric scooter rental, and local buses to various lakeside towns.
